requirements.requirement: Keep the population-specific fragment sizes, genome-copy input and allele-fraction scale distinct; recompute the fictional single-locus expectation with a target-allele probability, rather than silently treating it as tumour fraction.

evidence.passage: Scale: plasma DNA fragments show a pattern reminiscent of nuclease-cleaved nucleosomes with a peak at 166 base pairs (Lo 2010, in maternal plasma), and tumour-derived fragments are enriched at 90 to 150 base pairs (Mouliere 2018). One assay input in a breast-cancer comparison was 4,500 amplifiable copies, about 15 nanograms (Santonja 2023), and at about 3.3 picograms per haploid genome copy 1 nanogram is roughly 300 copies (arithmetic from genome size). In a fictional single-locus model with 4,500 amplifiable opportunities and target-allele probability 1 in 100,000, the expected target count is 0.045. The target-allele probability is not automatically a tumour-DNA fraction: copy number, variant multiplicity and clone representation matter.

evidence.passage: A worked limit: for multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 patient-specific structural variants on 4,500 amplifiable copies, the theoretical limit is 1 / (4,500 x variants), which is 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million, at 47 variants. The 4.7 parts per million detection rested on a single mutant molecule, and one sample not detected at 4,500 copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies (Santonja 2023). Whole-genome sequencing of cfDNA integrates thousands of mutations and reached tumour-fraction sensitivity as low as 10 to the minus 5 (Zviran 2020).

evidence.passage: ctDNA is a subset of cell-free DNA, and not every plasma variant is tumour-derived: in paired plasma and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis (Razavi 2019). requirements.requirement: Collection and processing: blood-cell breakdown before separation dilutes the tumour fraction; extraction retains only some molecules

evidence.passage: Collection conditions can change the mixture before testing: blood-cell breakdown adds genomic DNA and can dilute a tumour fraction. The NCI biospecimen practices document, revised February 2025, prefers plasma to serum. Its protocol recommends EDTA, accepts acid citrate dextrose, and advises avoiding heparin and citrate; the literature-summary section separately reports results with several anticoagulants when processing was immediate. For EDTA blood the protocol prefers centrifugation within 2 hours and accepts up to 4 hours at room temperature or 24 hours at 4 degrees Celsius; it recommends stabilising tubes for anticipated delays over 2 hours. These are recommendations for that specimen workflow, not a universal acceptance rule for every assay. Extraction and library preparation then retain only some available molecules, so the volume drawn is not the volume evaluated.

evidence.passage: Reading an assay report starts with the specimen and collection date, the plasma volume actually evaluated, DNA quality and recovery, origin checks, and the rule that turns a signal into a call. Low shedding, damaged input or failed quality controls can limit interpretation; a failed assay is a separate result from no qualifying signal. Genotyping, response monitoring and residual-disease detection are different intended uses. In its November 2024 drug-development guidance, FDA asks for validation of the complete workflow, representative clinical samples, the input range and prespecified calling cut-offs; validation of one use does not establish another.

evidence.passage: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. One established epithelial method captures with EpCAM, then checks cell shape, a nucleus, cytokeratin and absence of CD45, which is one operational definition and not a universal rule for all circulating tumour cells or tumour types. Physical methods select by size or deformability and remove or retain different cells, so marker independence is not unbiased recovery. A negative capture, such as zero qualifying cells in 7.5 mL, does not show that no tumour cells circulate and does not predict a ctDNA result, because free DNA fragments are a separate analyte.

requirements.requirement: Distinguish broader clonal haematopoiesis from the explicitly source-defined CHIP category and separate allele fractions from cell fractions.

evidence.passage: Clonal haematopoiesis (CH) is the broader phenomenon of blood-cell clones carrying acquired changes. In the 2022 WHO myeloid classification, CHIP requires a somatic mutation in a myeloid-malignancy-associated gene at a variant allele fraction of at least 2%, or at least 4% for X-linked gene mutations in males, without a diagnosed haematological disorder or unexplained cytopenia (Khoury 2022). Persistent unexplained cytopenia changes the classification question. These are criteria for a named category, not a rule that every smaller blood-cell clone is absent, tumour-derived or a sequencing error.
evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Distinguish broader clonal haematopoiesis from the explicitly source-defined CHIP category and separate allele fractions from cell fractions. Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.

evidence.passage: Reading the figures: a variant allele fraction counts variant alleles among the alleles evaluated and is not automatically the percentage of cells. Acquired (somatic) means not inherited and does not mean malignant. There is no age at which a plasma variant can simply be dismissed. Sequential samples show clones with DNA-damage-response mutations outgrowing others after radiation, platinum or topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure (Bolton 2020), which is selection of clones that can already be present and does not mean every new detection was caused by treatment.

requirements.requirement: Gene groups: DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1 with age (9.5% at 70 to 79); TP53, PPM1D, CHEK2 selected by therapy

evidence.passage: Which genes: in blood-cell exomes from 17,182 people most clonal variants fell in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, were rare before age 40, and were seen in 9.5% of people aged 70 to 79 (Jaiswal 2014). ASXL1 mutations were enriched in current or former smokers, and radiation, platinum and topoisomerase II inhibitors selected for DNA-damage-response genes (TP53, PPM1D, CHEK2), with sequential samples showing those clones outgrowing others after exposure (Bolton 2020). In 8,810 people with non-haematological cancers, PPM1D and TP53 mutations were associated with prior chemotherapy, and clonal haematopoiesis was found in 25% (Coombs 2017).

requirements.requirement: Discordance: blood molecular call and imaging result sample different material, regions, times and signals

evidence.passage:
A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. How much tumour DNA reaches the sampled blood varies between lesions, and recovery, background DNA, the features tracked and the assay's detection limit all shape the call. Imaging measures a defined region through a physical signal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the breast can report contrast enhancement or the volume of enhancing tissue, which is not a direct count of viable cancer cells. The two tests can therefore differ without either being wrong, and neither automatically replaces the other.

They can also share information. In Magbanua and colleagues' pilot of 84 women having neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, ctDNA concentration was correlated with MRI functional tumour volume at all four time points, with Spearman correlations of 0.42 to 0.49, and patients with detectable ctDNA had a higher median volume. Agreement was partial, and adding ctDNA early in treatment to volume-based prediction of pathological complete response gave only a numerical gain that was not statistically significant. ctDNA positivity after treatment added significantly to volume for predicting distant recurrence and death. A mismatch calls for checking dates, assay limits, the imaged region and the exact finding. It does not by itself show a false test or hidden metastatic disease.

requirements.requirement: Finite input: thousands of genome copies can leave no tumour molecule in the aliquot

evidence.passage: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

requirements.requirement: A ctDNA number is meaningful only with its measured quantity, unit and detection criteria

evidence.passage:
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) can be reported as a concentration, as a fraction, or as a yes or no call, and the three are not interchangeable. A concentration counts tumour-attributed molecules in a stated volume of plasma. One example is mean tumour molecules per millilitre (MTM/mL), which the I-SPY 2 breast-cancer study of Magbanua and colleagues used for ctDNA across tracked variants. A fraction divides tumour-attributed molecules by a stated total, such as all evaluated alleles at one position (variant allele fraction, VAF) or all evaluated DNA (an estimated tumour fraction). Parts per million (PPM) is a fraction multiplied by one million, so the number is only as meaningful as the fraction it scales: 0.01% is 100 PPM, and 0.00024% is 2.4 PPM, the lowest allele fraction Santonja and colleagues reported for ctDNA detection in breast cancer.

Concentration and fraction can move apart. If two equal one-millilitre aliquots each hold the same number of tumour molecules but one holds more background cell-free DNA, the concentration is unchanged and the fraction falls. A detection call and a reliable amount are also different claims, because the detection limit and the quantitation range are validated separately. Nothing here gives a conversion between assays: MTM/mL cannot be turned into PPM from the printed result, and a VAF of 100 PPM at one variant is not a tumour fraction of 100 PPM.

requirements.requirement: Define the observed interval between prespecified events and state who and which intervals enter its estimator.

evidence.passage:
In a ctDNA monitoring study, lead time is the date of a defined later event, such as confirmed clinical recurrence, minus the date of the first qualifying positive blood sample. The definition needs rules: whether recurrence means imaging, pathology or symptoms, whether the blood date is collection or reporting, whether a positive result triggered an extra scan, and whether treatment began on the signal. Blood draws and scans are both intermittent, so the observed gap reflects both schedules. A negative draw at month 3 and a first positive at month 6 do not locate when the signal began.

The denominator matters as much as the number. A median taken only over people with both an earlier positive and a later recurrence describes that selected group. It leaves out recurrences with no earlier positive, and people who are positive but have not recurred at the data cutoff have unfinished intervals, which are censored rather than zero or infinite. In García-Murillas and colleagues' prospective breast-cancer study, with blood taken every 3 months in the first year and every 6 months after, ctDNA detection preceded clinical relapse by a median of 10.7 months (95% CI 8.1 to 19.1) in the combined cohort of 144, and ctDNA found distant extracranial relapse in 22 of 23 patients but brain-only relapse in 1 of 6. In the c-TRAK TN trial, ctDNA was detected in 27.3% by 12 months and 7 patients relapsed without prior detection. A longer lead time shows earlier detection. It does not show that acting on the signal helps people live longer, which is the separate lead-time bias problem.
evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Define the observed interval between prespecified events and state who and which intervals enter its estimator. Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.

evidence.passage: Lead time is the interval between defined earlier and later detection events. Lead-time bias occurs when that timing difference is mistaken for a better outcome. requirements.requirement: Finite sampling: Poisson chance of zero is exp(minus lambda), 36.8% at an average of one; not a clinical false-negative rate (figure)

evidence.passage: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

requirements.requirement: Tumour-informed: features selected from a sampled tumour, tracked in later plasma; tumour-naive: predefined features and rules

evidence.passage: Tumour-informed assays (Signatera, RaDaR) sequence the resected tumour, choose a set of clonal mutations, and track them in plasma at high depth, which gives high specificity and lets a positive be called on very few molecules; the cost is a tumour sample, a bespoke panel per patient and a longer first turnaround. Tumour-naive assays (Guardant Reveal and most multi-cancer tests) apply a fixed panel of mutations and methylation or fragmentation features to every sample, so they work without tissue and from the first draw, at the price of having to distinguish tumour signal from clonal haematopoiesis and other background. Trials so far have used tumour-informed tests for treatment decisions (DYNAMIC used a tumour-informed approach; IMvigor011 used Signatera), while screening tests are necessarily tumour-naive. Head-to-head sensitivity comparisons are few, and results are not interchangeable between assays.

requirements.requirement: Why tracking many variants lowers the limit: 1/(copies x variants) = 4.7 ppm; whole-genome integration

evidence.passage: A worked limit: for multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 patient-specific structural variants on 4,500 amplifiable copies, the theoretical limit is 1 / (4,500 x variants), which is 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million, at 47 variants. The 4.7 parts per million detection rested on a single mutant molecule, and one sample not detected at 4,500 copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies (Santonja 2023). Whole-genome sequencing of cfDNA integrates thousands of mutations and reached tumour-fraction sensitivity as low as 10 to the minus 5 (Zviran 2020).

evidence.passage: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

requirements.requirement: ELISpot counts spots from cells secreting a chosen molecule under defined stimulation; it does not watch killing

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

evidence.passage: What the evidence does and does not support: the interferon gamma ELISpot is described as measuring the difference in the number of cells secreting the molecule with and without peptide, and interferon gamma is produced predominantly by natural killer and natural killer T cells as well as Th1 CD4 and CD8 effector T cells, so a mixed-cell spot does not by itself name the responding cell (Wykes and Renia protocol). In HIV vaccine research robust ELISpot responses were induced in a phase IIb trial that lacked efficacy, which challenged the assay's predictive power (Streeck 2009), and a validation in cynomolgus monkeys for responses to viral vector antigens (Yang 2022) validates that preparation and species and not cancer efficacy. Peptide added to cells can bypass the tumour's own processing and presentation, so a peptide response needs a separate bridge to natural tumour recognition.

evidence.passage: Flow cytometry measures features of prepared cells as they pass through an instrument. Immunophenotyping uses combinations of markers to distinguish cell populations, including in blood-cancer diagnosis and residual-disease testing. Other methods measure intracellular cytokines, degranulation or target-cell death. Primary method studies show that these are different readouts, and validation depends on preparation, panel, controls and analysis gates. The performance of one assay does not automatically validate every use of the platform.

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: light scatter and fluorescence from individual events in a prepared cell suspension, grouped by a chosen panel of stains. Input: whole blood, isolated cells or dissociated tissue, where preparation and staining use a defined aliquot and compatibility with later assays depends on fixation and other processing and tissue dissociation removes geography and can recover cell types unevenly. Output: event counts, percent of a named parent population, fluorescence in instrument-dependent units, and cells per volume only with a validated counting method. Controls: instrument checks, unstained and single-stain controls, viability, biological controls and fluorescence-minus-one controls for hard boundaries. Failure modes: dead cells, aggregates, weak markers, nonspecific staining, signal overlap, cell loss and inconsistent gates. It cannot tell unmeasured proteins, original tissue position, antigen specificity from general markers or benefit.

requirements.requirement: Panels, compensation and unmixing, gating; neither repairs a poor stain (Mermaid)

evidence.passage: What compensation does and does not do: in multicolour analysis spectral overlap between detectors needs compensation, and a mathematical and experimental analysis showed that photon-counting statistics add a nonlinear error to compensated parameters while measurement and log-scale binning errors add linear ones, most visibly with red and far-red fluorochromes where less light is emitted (Roederer 2001). Compensation or spectral unmixing therefore corrects overlap and does not repair a poorly chosen stain or set a positivity gate. The community guidelines (Cossarizza 2021) are methods guidance on preparation, panels and analysis and give no universal immune-response cut-off. A degranulation marker on the cell surface is an activity readout that accompanied cytolysis in antigen-specific CD8 T cells and is not itself measured target-cell death (Betts 2003).
evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Panels, compensation and unmixing, gating; neither repairs a poor stain (Mermaid) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.

evidence.passage: Gating is selection within recorded data, not physical collection. A typical analysis checks acquisition quality, excludes debris and cell pairs, assesses viability where the assay requires it, and identifies populations with a stated marker panel. Intracellular assays may assess viability before fixation; not every flow experiment studies living cells. Fluorescence-minus-one controls omit one stain while retaining the others and can help place a boundary, but do not establish antibody specificity. Tight earlier gates can discard unexpected or rare populations. Automated clusters still need biological and technical checks (Cossarizza 2021). A cell sorter can physically collect selected events for downstream work, subject to recovery, purity and functional-viability requirements; an analytical gate alone does not do this (Cossarizza 2019).

Nested gates show membership and not area, no cells per millilitre or whole-body total follows, and binding or marker identity does not show killing.

evidence.passage: Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

requirements.requirement: Background arithmetic: 40% raw death minus 30% target-only = 10 percentage points excess (figure)

evidence.passage: Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

requirements.requirement: Standardisation evidence: inter-laboratory variation falls with responding frequency; gating is a source of variability

evidence.passage: Precision evidence: in a study among laboratories involved in HIV clinical trials, using a common protocol and a cytomegalovirus pp65 peptide mix, mean inter-laboratory coefficients of variation ranged from 17% to 44% depending on sample type and analysis method, cryopreserved PBMC gave lower variation than whole blood, and centralised analysis with a dynamic gating template cut it by 5% to 20%. Variation was lowest (18% to 24%) for samples with more than 0.5% interferon gamma positive T cells and highest (57% to 82%) for samples below 0.1%, so gating is a major source of variability and precision falls as the responding frequency falls (Maecker 2005). That study supports protocol and gating consistency and does not validate every panel, stimulus or disease.

evidence.passage: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

requirements.requirement: Richness, Shannon entropy, normalised clonality, effective diversity: formulas and non-interchangeability

evidence.passage: Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Four clonotypes at 25, 25, 25 and 25 of 100 measured molecules give H = ln 4 = 1.386 and clonality 0. The same four at 70, 10, 10 and 10 give H = 0.940, clonality 1 minus 0.940 / 1.386 = 0.32, and an effective number of clonotypes exp(H) = 2.56. Richness is four in both, so many identities can coexist with strong dominance. Software may report Shannon entropy, its exponential or a normalised score, and these are not interchangeable: in the VDJtools documentation the Shannon-Wiener index returns the exponent of the entropy and the normalised index returns the entropy divided by the log of the clonotype count, which is evenness and not 1 minus that ratio, so a clonality built as 1 minus normalised entropy is a different number from either.
evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Richness, Shannon entropy, normalised clonality, effective diversity: formulas and non-interchangeability Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.

evidence.passage: Effective-diversity measures weight a distribution differently. For the inverse-Simpson convention, define D as the sum of squared clonotype fractions and report 1 / D: four equal fractions of 0.25 give 4, whereas 0.70, 0.10, 0.10 and 0.10 give 1 / 0.52, about 1.92. This differs from the Shannon effective diversity of about 2.56 for the same uneven distribution. A fictional sample containing only A and B at 50 molecules each has richness 2 and equal weights; low richness does not imply unequal weights.

evidence.passage: For one observed clonotype, the expression 1 minus H / ln K divides by ln 1, which is zero. Report how the software handles that case rather than silently applying the formula. Keep the software version, formula, filtering, input, compartment and abundance units, and inspect the distribution alongside the summary. Analytical reproducibility of a repertoire statistic does not establish a prognostic association or predict treatment benefit.

evidence.passage: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). evidence.passage: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. One established epithelial method captures with EpCAM, then checks cell shape, a nucleus, cytokeratin and absence of CD45, which is one operational definition and not a universal rule for all circulating tumour cells or tumour types. evidence.passage:
What it measures. CellSearch pulls circulating tumour cells out of 7.5 millilitres of blood with magnetic beads coated in an antibody to EpCAM, stains them for cytokeratin and a nuclear dye, excludes white cells with CD45, and counts the cells that pass. In metastatic breast cancer five or more cells, and in metastatic prostate and colorectal cancer five or three, mark an unfavourable group.

Evidence. The 2004 New England Journal of Medicine study in metastatic breast cancer showed that women with five or more cells before starting a new treatment had far shorter progression-free and overall survival, and the FDA cleared the system the same year, then for prostate and colorectal cancer in 2008. The count also tracks response: a fall below the threshold after one cycle is a good sign. The disappointment was SWOG S0500, which switched chemotherapy early in women whose count stayed high and found no survival gain, so the count is prognostic rather than a guide to which drug to use. In hormone receptor positive breast cancer the French STIC CTC trial used the count to choose between endocrine therapy and chemotherapy and found the strategy non-inferior to the physician's choice.

Who should have it and what changes. Guidelines do not recommend routine CellSearch counts because no decision has been shown to improve outcomes from them, so use is mainly in trials and in centres studying circulating cells, where the captured cells can also be stained for HER2, androgen receptor variants or PD-L1. The test is available through Menarini Silicon Biosystems and reference laboratories at a cost similar to a specialised blood test. CellSearch pulls circulating tumour cells out of 7.5 millilitres of blood with magnetic beads coated in an antibody to EpCAM, stains them for cytokeratin and a nuclear dye, excludes white cells with CD45, and counts the cells that pass. The 2004 New England Journal of Medicine study in metastatic breast cancer showed that women with five or more cells before starting a new treatment had far shorter progression-free and overall survival, and the FDA cleared the system the same year, then for prostate and colorectal cancer in 2008. The count also tracks response: a fall below the threshold after one cycle is a good sign. The disappointment was SWOG S0500, which switched chemotherapy early in women whose count stayed high and found no survival gain, so the count is prognostic rather than a guide to which drug to use. In hormone receptor positive breast cancer the French STIC CTC trial used the count to choose between endocrine therapy and chemotherapy and found the strategy non-inferior to the physician's choice.

evidence.passage:
What it does. Blood flows through a stepped microfluidic channel whose gaps narrow to a few micrometres. Large, stiff tumour cells are held in the steps while smaller, deformable blood cells pass. Reversing the flow releases the trapped cells intact, so they can be counted, stained, cultured or sequenced. Because the capture depends on physical properties rather than EpCAM, it also holds mesenchymal-like and cluster cells that antibody systems miss.

Regulatory status and evidence. In May 2022 the FDA granted De Novo authorisation to the Parsortix PC1 system for capturing and harvesting circulating tumour cells from the blood of patients with metastatic breast cancer for later analysis; it is CE marked in Europe. The clearance covers harvesting, not any specific clinical claim, so the downstream test decides what the cells mean. ANGLE, the developer, has built assays on the harvested cells for HER2, androgen receptor variants and DNA damage response markers and offers them as a service to pharmaceutical trials.

Who should have it and what changes. Nothing changes in routine care yet: harvested cells feed research and trial biomarkers rather than approved treatment decisions. Its promise is access to live tumour cells without a biopsy, for example to test protein targets that DNA cannot show, such as HER2 or oestrogen receptor on metastatic cells, and to grow cells for functional testing. Availability is through ANGLE's laboratories and partner sites; cost is that of a specialised research assay.

evidence.passage: Measure, then infer: the measured features are fragment length, end sequences, genomic positions and chemical marks. A reference or trained model then turns them into a source estimate or a score, so the output is an inference and not a cell census, and no single fragment carries a cancer address. evidence.passage:
In a ctDNA monitoring study, lead time is the date of a defined later event, such as confirmed clinical recurrence, minus the date of the first qualifying positive blood sample. The definition needs rules: whether recurrence means imaging, pathology or symptoms, whether the blood date is collection or reporting, whether a positive result triggered an extra scan, and whether treatment began on the signal. Blood draws and scans are both intermittent, so the observed gap reflects both schedules. A negative draw at month 3 and a first positive at month 6 do not locate when the signal began.

The denominator matters as much as the number. A median taken only over people with both an earlier positive and a later recurrence describes that selected group. It leaves out recurrences with no earlier positive, and people who are positive but have not recurred at the data cutoff have unfinished intervals, which are censored rather than zero or infinite. In García-Murillas and colleagues' prospective breast-cancer study, with blood taken every 3 months in the first year and every 6 months after, ctDNA detection preceded clinical relapse by a median of 10.7 months (95% CI 8.1 to 19.1) in the combined cohort of 144, and ctDNA found distant extracranial relapse in 22 of 23 patients but brain-only relapse in 1 of 6. In the c-TRAK TN trial, ctDNA was detected in 27.3% by 12 months and 7 patients relapsed without prior detection. A longer lead time shows earlier detection. It does not show that acting on the signal helps people live longer, which is the separate lead-time bias problem.

evidence.passage: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

evidence.passage: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

evidence.passage: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. Blood-cancer studies can use cell-based or molecular measurements, while solid-tumour studies can look for tumour-associated features in plasma. Associations with recurrence, benefit from a test-guided treatment strategy, and validation of a surrogate endpoint are separate questions; evidence for one setting does not establish the others.

As a genome-wide readout it sits under no target.

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. evidence.passage: What the evidence does and does not support: the interferon gamma ELISpot is described as measuring the difference in the number of cells secreting the molecule with and without peptide, and interferon gamma is produced predominantly by natural killer and natural killer T cells as well as Th1 CD4 and CD8 effector T cells, so a mixed-cell spot does not by itself name the responding cell (Wykes and Renia protocol). In HIV vaccine research robust ELISpot responses were induced in a phase IIb trial that lacked efficacy, which challenged the assay's predictive power (Streeck 2009), and a validation in cynomolgus monkeys for responses to viral vector antigens (Yang 2022) validates that preparation and species and not cancer efficacy. Peptide added to cells can bypass the tumour's own processing and presentation, so a peptide response needs a separate bridge to natural tumour recognition.

evidence.passage: What compensation does and does not do: in multicolour analysis spectral overlap between detectors needs compensation, and a mathematical and experimental analysis showed that photon-counting statistics add a nonlinear error to compensated parameters while measurement and log-scale binning errors add linear ones, most visibly with red and far-red fluorochromes where less light is emitted (Roederer 2001). The community guidelines (Cossarizza 2021) are methods guidance on preparation, panels and analysis and give no universal immune-response cut-off. evidence.passage: Gating is selection within recorded data, not physical collection. A typical analysis checks acquisition quality, excludes debris and cell pairs, assesses viability where the assay requires it, and identifies populations with a stated marker panel. Intracellular assays may assess viability before fixation; not every flow experiment studies living cells. Fluorescence-minus-one controls omit one stain while retaining the others and can help place a boundary, but do not establish antibody specificity. Tight earlier gates can discard unexpected or rare populations. Automated clusters still need biological and technical checks (Cossarizza 2021). A cell sorter can physically collect selected events for downstream work, subject to recovery, purity and functional-viability requirements; an analytical gate alone does not do this (Cossarizza 2019).

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.

evidence.passage: Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.

evidence.passage: Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

evidence.passage: Precision evidence: in a study among laboratories involved in HIV clinical trials, using a common protocol and a cytomegalovirus pp65 peptide mix, mean inter-laboratory coefficients of variation ranged from 17% to 44% depending on sample type and analysis method, cryopreserved PBMC gave lower variation than whole blood, and centralised analysis with a dynamic gating template cut it by 5% to 20%. Variation was lowest (18% to 24%) for samples with more than 0.5% interferon gamma positive T cells and highest (57% to 82%) for samples below 0.1%, so gating is a major source of variability and precision falls as the responding frequency falls (Maecker 2005). That study supports protocol and gating consistency and does not validate every panel, stimulus or disease.

evidence.passage: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. How: HLA molecules are assembled with the selected peptide and several copies are attached to a labelled scaffold (a tetramer is one format), cells are exposed and analysed, usually by flow cytometry, with viable-cell and gate selection. Input: blood or tissue cells, where staining uses a defined aliquot and compatibility with later living-cell assays depends on the preparation, and the reagent must match both peptide and allele. Thresholds: gate and positivity rules need background and reagent controls, and no universal percentage shows efficacy. Failure modes: nonspecific binding, weak binding, dead cells, a wrong or poorly formed reagent, chain differences or sampling loss. It cannot tell cytokine response, tumour-cell killing, healthy-tissue specificity or benefit.

evidence.passage: What the evidence shows: in the original report, tetramers of HLA-A2 with two HIV-derived peptides or an influenza A matrix peptide bound peptide-specific cytotoxic T cells in vitro and T cells from the blood of HIV-infected people, and binding in general correlated well with cytotoxicity assays (Altman 1996). That is a correlation in those systems and not a rule that binding equals killing for an arbitrary tumour peptide. Tetramers are made by mixing biotinylated MHC with fluorescent streptavidin, and a later method made them with small-molecule fluorophores (Ramachandiran 2007), so reagent preparation is a source of variation. An observed stain shows binding under the tested conditions and does not show natural processing and display of that pair by a tumour.

evidence.passage: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

evidence.passage: Measurement card: input is a sequencing-derived clonotype table and the calculation consumes no further tissue, though the upstream assay consumes its sample. Output units are a count for richness, dimensionless values for entropy and normalised clonality, and an effective clonotype count for effective diversity. Controls are matched compartments and handling, chain definition, error filtering, abundance units (reads, corrected molecules or cells are not automatically equivalent), depth assessment and replicates or resampling. Subsampling to a comparable depth helps assess sampling effects but cannot recover cells never sampled. A clonality summary does not identify what the receptors recognise, whether cells killed tumour, or whether treatment helped, and there is no universal clonality score that means an immune therapy is working.

evidence.passage: Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Four clonotypes at 25, 25, 25 and 25 of 100 measured molecules give H = ln 4 = 1.386 and clonality 0. The same four at 70, 10, 10 and 10 give H = 0.940, clonality 1 minus 0.940 / 1.386 = 0.32, and an effective number of clonotypes exp(H) = 2.56. Richness is four in both, so many identities can coexist with strong dominance. Software may report Shannon entropy, its exponential or a normalised score, and these are not interchangeable: in the VDJtools documentation the Shannon-Wiener index returns the exponent of the entropy and the normalised index returns the entropy divided by the log of the clonotype count, which is evenness and not 1 minus that ratio, so a clonality built as 1 minus normalised entropy is a different number from either.

evidence.passage: Effective-diversity measures weight a distribution differently. For the inverse-Simpson convention, define D as the sum of squared clonotype fractions and report 1 / D: four equal fractions of 0.25 give 4, whereas 0.70, 0.10, 0.10 and 0.10 give 1 / 0.52, about 1.92. This differs from the Shannon effective diversity of about 2.56 for the same uneven distribution. A fictional sample containing only A and B at 50 molecules each has richness 2 and equal weights; low richness does not imply unequal weights.

evidence.passage: Assay card: measures receptor identities, usually by the complementarity-determining region 3 of the variable region, and their measured representation in the sampled population. How: extract nucleic acid, amplify or capture receptor regions, sequence, then group and count under stated rules, which may use nucleotide or amino-acid sequence, gene segments, one chain or paired chains. Input: blood cells or tissue nucleic acid for bulk methods and compatible cell preparations for single-cell methods, and preparation consumes material. A high-resolution human repertoire method reported chain diversity without sequence-associated or quantitative restrictions (Ruggiero 2015). Failure modes: poor material, shallow sampling, amplification bias, chain mismatch, inconsistent definitions and batch effects. It cannot tell every receptor's target, tissue position, killing or benefit, and a research method is not automatically a treatment-selection test.

evidence.passage: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

evidence.passage: Source attribution in plasma, interpretation rule: TP53 is a tumour gene and also a therapy-selected blood-cell gene, so a TP53 variant in plasma after chemotherapy can come from either compartment. Matched white-blood-cell DNA and the tumour's variant list, where available, help assess its origin; some variants remain ambiguous. In Razavi's paired sequencing 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 controls without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, and variants that could not be separated from white-blood-cell DNA kept an explicit ambiguous category, so subtracting every blood match is not a complete attribution method.

evidence.passage: Fictional example: a plasma assay detects a variant that sensitive matched blood-cell sequencing finds at 0.8% VAF. The blood result supports a blood-cell contribution even below the 2% cut-off, but it does not make the variant CHIP or exclude a tumour contribution, because tumour evidence, shared variants and each method's limits still apply. Matched sequencing has its own gene coverage, depth and detection rules, so a clone below its sensitivity can stay unseen, and a clone finding is not a leukaemia diagnosis or a solid-tumour treatment instruction.

evidence.passage: How common it is: in paired plasma and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, and variants that could not be separated from white-blood-cell DNA kept an explicit ambiguous category (Razavi 2019). Blood-cell clones also fall into gene groups: DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1 with age (Jaiswal 2014) and TP53, PPM1D and CHEK2 selected by radiation, platinum and topoisomerase II inhibitors (Bolton 2020). A gene often mutated in tumours is therefore not proof of tumour origin.
